selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The America's Living Library Act establishes a pilot program under the Department of the Interior to collect, catalog, and sequence genomic data from animals, plants, fungi, and microbes found in units of the National Park System. The bill provides authorization of appropriations over several fiscal years for program oversight, genome sequencing, sample storage, and data storage across multiple federal entities and the Smithsonian Institution. It also sets data standards, site selection criteria, sample retention and safety rules, tribal consultation requirements, and eventual reporting and termination rules.

affected_groups.effect: The Department of the Interior, Department of Agriculture, National Institutes of Health, and the Smithsonian Institution receive specific funding and interagency coordination duties to collect, store, sequence, and manage genomic data and physical samples.
Subject to engagement in formal tribal consultation during the implementation of the program.

Eligible to provide in-kind contributions for resources and materials under conflict-of-interest vetting, and gain access to genomic data and non-public services for artificial intelligence model training under restrictions excluding foreign entities of concern.

key_provisions: Establishes the America's Living Library Project pilot program within the United States Geological Survey to facilitate the collection of new genomic data from species found in the National Park System.
Requires the initial selection of 5 National Park System units within 180 days of enactment, followed by an additional 20 units within 2 years.
Mandates the creation of a publicly available genomic database that withholds personally identifiable information and sensitive collection locality coordinates.
Prohibits the transfer, export, or loan of physical samples outside the United States and requires all physical storage, curation, and laboratory processing to occur within domestic facilities.

Authorizes specific multi-year appropriations from fiscal years 2027 through 2031 for the Department of the Interior, the Smithsonian Institution, the Department of Agriculture, and the National Institutes of Health.
Terminates the program authority 10 years after the date of enactment.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The America's Living Library Act establishes a pilot program under the Department of the Interior to collect, catalog, and sequence genomic data from animals, plants, fungi, and microbes found in units of the National Park System. The bill provides authorization of appropriations over several fiscal years for program oversight, genome sequencing, sample storage, and data storage across multiple federal entities and the Smithsonian Institution. It also sets data standards, site selection criteria, sample retention and safety rules, tribal consultation requirements, and eventual reporting and termination rules.
summary_detail.significance: The bill creates a focused federal scientific pilot program spanning multiple agencies to map the genomic data of species living across selected national parks, backed by specific multi-year funding authorizations totaling tens of millions of dollars annually. It impacts federal scientific research, interagency biological data management, conservation storage infrastructure, and rules governing access to domestic genetic information.
